To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the presence of reduced sediments in an alluvial aquifier can prevent the mobilization of uranium, (2) the redox-buffer capacity of reduced sedients in this system is overwhelmed by an influx of dissolved O2, (3) U is mobilized when redox buffering is overwhelmed, and (4) the redox buffering capacity of reduced sediment can be restored after the influx of dissolved O, but only if the rate of dissolved O2 delivery is decreased.
